item.title: Chinese Tech Firms Expand Globally with AI Innovations
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: How Chinese companies are taking innovation global
Chinese companies are expanding globally by applying AI to diverse needs, facing challenges in adapting products to new markets. Voiskey.ai and Wanderboat demonstrate how AI can address different user requirements, but success depends on understanding local habits, expectations, and infrastructure. Cloud services like AWS provide technical support by offering scalable resources and connections to local developers, customers, and partners. International expansion requires flexibility to handle varying traffic, regulatory demands, and user preferences. Companies must balance technical innovation with market-specific adjustments, such as payment habits and convenience expectations. Local ecosystems and partnerships are critical for long-term presence, as relationships with developers and businesses reveal practical barriers and opportunities. AWS facilitates these connections, enabling companies to engage with communities and refine their approaches. The broader goal is not just exporting products but building relevance through mutual learning and adapting to new markets' needs.

item.title: Huawei launches desktop PCs with domestically made components and HarmonyOS
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Huawei develops 'entirely Chinese' homegrown desktop PC system
Huawei has launched its first desktop PCs, the Qinyun HM650 and HM650g, featuring its 10-core Kirin X90 processor and HarmonyOS Enterprise Edition operating system. The machines include 16 GB LPDDR5 memory and 256GB or 512GB SSDs, with components sourced from Chinese manufacturers like CXMT and YMTC. The Kirin X90, built using SMIC's 7nm-class N+2 process, integrates Huawei's Taishan CPU cores, Maleoon GPU, and a neural processing unit for AI. While Huawei claims all components are domestically manufactured, teardowns reveal reliance on foreign equipment, materials, and software tools from the Netherlands, U.S., Japan, and UK. HarmonyOS Enterprise Edition replaces Windows, using Huawei's proprietary kernel and architecture, but may lack compatibility with Windows applications. Huawei asserts full domestic production, though the semiconductor supply chain still depends on global tools and IP. The system represents progress in domestic chip development but faces challenges in complete self-reliance and software compatibility.

item.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.2.1 Security Update for iMessage, AirPlay, Bluetooth
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Don't Ignore iOS 27.2.1: Your iPhone Gets iMessage, AirPlay Security Fixes
Apple released iOS 27.2.1 and iPadOS 27.2.1 updates to address security vulnerabilities in iMessage, AirPlay, and Bluetooth. The iMessage fixes prevent attackers from remotely joining group chats and viewing messages, with separate vulnerabilities allowing pre-join message access. Bluetooth issues let malicious devices bypass pairing limits and pair secretly, risking memory corruption. AirPlay vulnerabilities could enable unauthorized connections. The update also resolves a flaw in Apple's App Intents platform that could expose sensitive user data. Apple advises users to update to the latest iOS version via Settings > General > Software Update. The next major iOS update, iOS 27.3, is expected in December, with developer previews hinting at new features like StandBy Mode for iPhone Duo and self-recording karaoke mode in Apple Music.

item.title: Microsoft Adds Option to Permanently Disable Sticky Keys Pop-Up in Windows 11
item.description:
Source: Engadget, PCMag Original headline: Microsoft Introduces Option to Permanently Disable Sticky Keys Pop-Up in Windows 11
Microsoft is adding a feature in Windows 11 that lets users permanently disable the Sticky Keys pop-up. The update includes a checkbox labeled 'Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut' in the existing prompt that appears after pressing Shift five times. This change addresses frustration among gamers and power users who rely on Shift for actions like sprinting or walking in games. The feature is currently available only to Windows Insider Program participants in builds 26340.9882 and 26320.9876, with plans to expand to all users. Users can also disable Sticky Keys via Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard. The Sticky Keys feature, part of Windows since 1995, aids users needing multi-key shortcuts without simultaneous presses. While the pop-up remains useful for some, the new option provides greater control for those who prefer to avoid it. The update reflects Microsoft's efforts to refine accessibility settings and reduce interruptions for general users.

item.title: AMD to Surpass Intel in Revenue for First Time on AI Demand
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: AMD says it will outsell Intel for the first time in its history as Epyc and Instinct sales soar on AI demand
AMD expects Q4 2026 revenue of $17 billion, surpassing Intel's $15–16 billion forecast for the first time. Data center sales nearly doubled to $8.5 billion, driven by Instinct MI455X GPUs and Helios racks. AMD's revenue lead stems from AI demand, not volume, as Intel still ships two-thirds of x86 CPUs. CEO Lisa Su noted first-quarter revenue from Instinct accelerators and 2nm Epyc processors, though full Venice stack shipments are delayed until 2027. Intel's guidance includes a $300 million revenue hit from a Fab 28 explosion, reducing its projected revenue to $16.3 billion. AMD's data center segment, now 64% of total sales, is set to outperform Intel's AI group, which earned $7.3 billion in Q3 2026. AMD's CFO Jean Hu projects data center revenue to rise 50% sequentially to $12.8 billion in Q4, with AI accelerators overtaking server CPUs. Intel's data center group grew 78% year-over-year but trails AMD. AMD faces inventory and cash flow challenges, with data centers expected to account for over 80% of revenue in 2027. The shift reflects industry-wide demand for AI accelerators, not a CPU market win.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Steam Deck now shows FPS data for games on Steam Store
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Steam Deck owners can finally see how badly a game runs before buying it
Valve is introducing a feature for Steam Deck owners to check real-world performance data before purchasing games. Starting November 10, the Steam Store page will display average frames per second (FPS) for titles, collected from other players’ performance statistics. The data appears under Steam Deck Compatibility > Learn more, available for Verified, Playable, and Unsupported games. A histogram shows frame-rate frequency, highlighting inconsistencies in average FPS. Valve notes existing compatibility labels don’t always align with user expectations, as some Unsupported games may run smoothly for some players, while Verified titles might struggle. Performance data is limited to default frame rates (60 FPS for LCD, 90 FPS for OLED) and excludes graphics settings, reflecting varied configurations. The feature will expand beyond Steam Deck, with desktop beta users invited to contribute data. This update aims to reduce uncertainty in selecting games for the device’s growing library.

item.title: Lubrizol Uses AI to Boost Chemical R&D Efficiency
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
Lubrizol, a specialty chemicals manufacturer, is integrating AI and digital tools to enhance R&D efficiency. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology, emphasizes building a digital foundation that connects business processes, data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support researchers. The goal is to combine decades of technical data with chemists' expertise to accelerate idea testing, improve decision-making, and develop sustainable materials without compromising performance. Data scientists help identify patterns and model possibilities before physical experiments, though Rao stresses AI complements, rather than replaces, scientific judgment. Fusion teams of scientists, data scientists, and IT professionals collaborate on shared objectives, starting with small pilots to build trust. Cloud infrastructure provides flexibility to access computing resources without heavy investments. Digital modeling aids sustainability efforts by evaluating alternative materials and assessing lifecycle trade-offs. Scaling production remains challenging, but AI's ability to model variables could help balance performance, regulatory, and financial demands. Rao anticipates AI, automation, and digital twins will converge to create intelligent labs and efficient manufacturing, requiring responsible integration of these technologies at scale.

item.title: Nvidia Restricts Overseas GPU Rentals to China
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China
Nvidia has restricted overseas cloud GPU rentals to China, requiring at least 51% of its services to go to non-Chinese firms. Chinese AI labs, facing export bans, have purchased over 1 million Nvidia cards this year and are leasing abroad, with some deals offering 30-50% higher upfront payments. A B300 rack sold for $2.8 million in China, compared to $600,000 globally. Chinese firms have ordered 6.6 million export-compliant RTX Pro 5500 cards, exceeding Nvidia’s 2027 production capacity. Domestic alternatives like Huawei’s Ascend 910C lag behind Nvidia’s CUDA-supported chips. Companies like Moonshot and Tencent are seeking overseas leases, including European Blackwell GPUs, while the Remote Access Security Act (RASA) could expand U.S. export controls. Nvidia’s Q3 results on Nov. 17 may clarify the impact of its 51% rule, which faces scrutiny amid CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged spy investigation. Demand for GPUs far exceeds supply, with domestic production hitting 3.5 million units this year against a 5 million demand. Legal hurdles and export restrictions complicate both ownership and leasing options for Chinese firms.

item.title: TSA may ask travelers to power on phones for safety checks
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The safety reason TSA might ask you to turn on your phone
TSA agents may ask travelers to turn on their phones during security checks to confirm they are functioning devices. This rule, in place since 2014, aims to ensure phones are not used as detonators, jamming devices, or to store bomb components. Travelers from overseas must power on devices to prove functionality, though most will not face this. CBP can conduct routine phone inspections under border search exceptions, inspecting text messages and app activity without a warrant. With reasonable suspicion, agents may perform thorough inspections. A 2025 proposal allows CBP to request five-year social media history from certain travelers, though it remains a proposal. If asked to power on a phone, travelers should unlock it to demonstrate it is a working device. TSA agents are within their rights to require this, while CBP inspections may involve more extensive checks for international travelers.

item.title: Laptop overheating: Causes and cooling tips
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The reason your laptop can get hot after extended use
Laptops generate heat from internal components like the processor and battery, packed into a compact chassis. Prolonged use or resource-intensive tasks, such as gaming or video editing, increase temperatures. Background processes and software updates also contribute to heat buildup. Normal operation includes fan activation and CPU/GPU throttling to manage temperatures. Excessive heat can cause freezing or restarts, indicating potential issues. Airflow is critical; using laptops on soft surfaces or in high ambient temperatures exacerbates overheating. Apple recommends keeping MacBooks between 50-95°F, while Microsoft notes Surface fans activate above 77°F. To cool laptops, ensure vents are unblocked, use cooling pads, clean vents, and close resource-heavy programs. Task Manager (Windows) or Activity Monitor (Mac) can identify CPU-heavy processes. If issues persist, check for fan blockages, dried thermal paste, or consider software downgrades for older laptops. Severe cases require technical support.

item.title: Pentagon Considers Lunar Satellite Fleet for Strategic Reach
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Pentagon mulls placing fleet of military satellites around the Moon
The US military has issued a Request for Information seeking to deploy an unspecified number of satellites in a 'proliferated cislunar constellation' around the Moon. The move follows statements by Space Force acquisitions chief Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, who emphasized the Pentagon's growing focus on lunar operations. Purdy cited an executive order from President Donald Trump's administration, which framed cislunar space as a critical domain for detecting and countering threats to US interests. He told industry representatives that the Moon is now a 'warfighting domain,' urging collaboration on lunar initiatives. Officials note the strategic importance of the Moon as the US and China advance lunar programs, with competition over access to water ice at the south pole and limited landing zones. The satellites aim to protect US interests amid rising geopolitical tensions in space.

item.title: Adobe and Disney Partner on AI Tools for Storytelling
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Adobe and Disney team up to build AI tools for the next generation of storytelling
Adobe and The Walt Disney Company have launched a multi-year partnership focused on advancing storytelling and creativity through AI. The collaboration includes Adobe providing Disney with early access to tools like Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, and Photoshop, along with engineers and researchers. Firefly Foundry will help Disney develop generative AI models trained on its intellectual property, enabling safe and commercially viable content creation. Disney’s Imagineering team is already using the tool to convert hand-drawn sketches into finished 2D art and generate images matching franchise aesthetics. The partnership also involves StudioLAB, where Adobe supports innovation in creative workflows, and ESPN Edge, exploring AI-driven sports fan engagement. Joint projects have begun, with additional initiatives planned over the next few years.

item.title: Earth Microbe Survives Mars-Like Toxins, Begins Reproducing
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Scientists Gave an Earth Microbe Toxins Found on Mars. It Started Multiplying
Scientists tested the Earth microbe Haloferax volcanii under Mars-like conditions, including perchlorate and nitrate toxins, low pressure, high salt, and oxygen-free environments for 160 days. The extremophile survived and reproduced, albeit slower than Earth conditions, while retaining water via biofilms. Lead researcher Adam Robinson of the University of Florida noted the simulated environment, though not fully replicating all Martian conditions, demonstrates life as we know it could thrive in potential Mars-like settings. The study, published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, highlights that the microbes used Martian toxins for metabolism. While the experiment excluded factors like extreme subsurface temperatures, Robinson argues the findings support expanding the search for current microbial life on Mars. The research adds to evidence suggesting life might exist beneath the planet's surface today.

item.title: Anthropic Still Plans to Go Public Despite Wall Street Concerns
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Anthropic Still Plans to Go Public as Soon as Next Week: Report
Anthropic plans to go public on Nasdaq as early as Oct. 19 or 20, per Wall Street Journal. The company’s valuation has shifted from earlier speculation of $2 trillion to a more realistic range of $1.5 trillion to $1.25 trillion. Tech stocks, including Nvidia, have declined sharply this month, with shares dropping from $243.37 to $178.67. Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, faces scrutiny over alleged ties to a Chinese spy, prompting President Trump to say the FBI is investigating. Anthropic’s regulatory filings note AI could pose catastrophic risks, though investors are concerned about an AI arms race enabling powerful hacking tools. Competitor OpenAI plans to go public but not before year-end. Anthropic reported $33 billion in revenue from January to September 2026.

item.title: Venmo launches in-app bill splitting with receipt scanning
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Venmo finally launches an in-app bill splitting feature
Venmo has launched an in-app bill splitting feature that scans receipts, itemizes bills, and splits payments among users. The tool automatically calculates tax and tips, compiling them into a payment request within the app. The feature is rolling out now and will be widely available in a few weeks. Venmo’s receipt scanning capability works across all mobile devices, offering a streamlined alternative to manual calculations. The update follows Apple’s Visual Intelligence feature, which allows iPhone users to split bills via Apple Cash. Venmo’s general manager, Alexis Sowa, noted that bill splitting is common but often tedious, and the new tool eliminates the need for manual math. The feature adds pressure on users who prefer competing apps like Cash App or Zelle, as friends already on Venmo can now split bills seamlessly within the app.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Linux SSH Vulnerability
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
Hackers are exploiting a critical Linux vulnerability named *sshole, which allows unauthenticated access to privileged accounts via OpenSSH and musl. The flaw, disclosed last Thursday, has already seen active attacks, with security firm Greynoise reporting intrusions by group GT10. The attackers, using AI-generated backdoors with Chinese comments, deploy Python3 to run TAC Agent, a tool enabling shell commands, system reconnaissance, and persistence. Greynoise identified the group’s mature intrusions targeting honeypots in Southeast Asia, revealing potential victims and attack methods. OpenSSH has released a patch to mitigate the vulnerability. The breach highlights risks to Linux systems relying on the affected software combination.

item.title: Gmail Users Can Undo Sent Emails with Time Limit
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Gmail users should know about this little-noticed feature
Gmail users can undo sent emails within a short time window. After sending, a pop-up appears offering 'Undo' and 'View message' options. The 'Undo' function delays email delivery but does not remove it from the recipient's inbox. Users have seconds to act, with the default undo period set to five seconds. This delay prevents the email from being sent immediately but does not notify the recipient. The undo window can be extended to 10, 20, or 30 seconds via Gmail settings. To adjust, users access 'See all settings' in the General settings page under 'Undo Send.' Changes require saving to take effect. Emails already sent cannot be retrieved once they reach the recipient's inbox. The feature is designed to allow last-minute corrections before emails are dispatched.

item.title: Uber Launches Parking Booking Feature
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Uber Now Lets You Book Parking Spots
Uber is adding a parking reservation feature to its app, allowing users to book spots in supported locations. The new Parking tab lets users search by location, date, and duration, displaying pricing upfront. Filters let users choose between self-park, valet, covered garages, and open-air lots. Booking requires car details and payment, followed by a QR code for verification. Users can cancel free before their slot or extend at a fee. Uber One members earn 10% credits on bookings. The feature follows Uber's acquisition of SpotHero, which lists over 13,000 parking options across 400 U.S. and Canadian cities.

item.title: YouTube Returns to Billboard Charts in 2027
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch Original headline: YouTube Returns to Billboard Charts in 2027 Amid Updated Streaming Metrics
YouTube will resume sharing streaming data with Billboard charts starting in 2027 after revised metrics better reflect engagement with ad-supported platforms. The decision ends a dispute that began in December 2025, when YouTube halted data sharing due to Billboard’s outdated focus on paid subscriptions. Billboard’s 2026 formula reduces the gap between paid and ad-supported streams, valuing 1,500 ad streams as one album consumption unit—equivalent to 1,000 paid streams—down from 2,500 previously. YouTube’s global head of music, Lyor Cohen, had criticized the old system in 2025, arguing it ignored free streaming’s role in discovery and revenue, which accounts for 84% of U.S. recorded music revenue. The updated metric balances paid and ad streams, with paid listens still carrying more weight. The change benefits artists, particularly independents and those with international fanbases, as YouTube’s data includes music videos, lyric videos, and live performances. Billboard’s revised approach provides a broader view of music consumption, reflecting shifting listener habits and the growing importance of ad-supported services.

item.title: Medium Launches AI Writing App to Assist with Content Creation
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Medium’s new TK app brings AI assistance directly into the writing process
Medium launched its new TK app, integrating AI assistance directly into the writing process. The app allows users to request help by typing '@TK' followed by a prompt, offering features like answering factual questions, pulling in saved text, and providing editorial feedback. TK repurposes the traditional placeholder 'TK' (meaning 'to come') to signify AI-generated content. The company acknowledges growing concerns in publishing about AI's role in writing, including disputes over authorship and AI detection reliability. Medium argues AI can enhance, not replace, human writing, emphasizing transparency by letting authors disclose AI use. The app includes tools for organizing past work, generating prompts, and connecting to external AI agents. It is free for Medium users, available web-based with a desktop version planned. Medium stresses collaboration and accessibility, with no encryption but access controls for work. The launch highlights ongoing debates about AI's impact on creative writing and content authenticity.

item.title: Microsoft's next Windows update will be 27H2, not Windows 12
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: The next big Windows update isn’t Windows 12
Microsoft released Windows 11 26H2, a smaller update with fewer new features than expected. The company is now developing 27H2, the next Windows 11 version, which will not be labeled as Windows 12. Insiders describe 27H2 as a 'comprehensive redesign' focused on 'quality,' potentially overhauling core components similar to the 24H2 update. Microsoft has not officially announced 27H2, but experts speculate the name change avoids high expectations tied to a new major version. Upcoming updates are expected to follow incremental improvements and prioritize community feedback. The company’s strategy remains unproven, with uncertainty about its success.

item.title: Lawyer Builds Private AI Server Using Eight Used Nvidia V100 GPUs
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Lawyer builds private AI server with eight used Nvidia V100 GPUs
A lawyer built a private AI server using eight used Nvidia V100-SXM2-32GB GPUs to handle legal case files internally. The system, configured with two NVLink-connected boards and four PEX switches, runs the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model, achieving up to 215 tokens per second. The GPUs, originally purchased for $2,400 each, now trade for $900 on eBay. The setup includes a Gigabyte Threadripper Pro motherboard, 8x 32GB DDR4 RAM, and two 2,800W power supplies. The server processes case data, summarizes records, and drafts legal documents without external data leaks. The builder notes that splitting model layers across GPUs improved performance, avoiding PCIe bottlenecks. Challenges included power limits, ECC errors, and hardware compatibility issues, resolved by capping GPU clocks and adjusting RAM speeds. The system handles one request at a time but aims to scale to multiple tasks. It reduces reliance on cloud models, saving costs while protecting client data. The lawyer plans to expand the setup with a second server and potentially commercialize the project.

item.title: Scientists use game theory to predict alien contact attempts
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Scientists turn to game theory in their search for alien life
Scientists at the SETI Institute are using game theory to predict when an alien civilization might attempt to contact Earth. Researchers Isabel Gerrard and Sofia Sheikh propose that intelligent civilizations might use a Schelling point—a shared decision without communication—to identify astronomical events significant enough to send messages. They suggest the antisolar point, the direction opposite the Sun from Earth, as a potential meeting point. This location allows an alien civilization to observe Earth passing in front of the Sun, a method astronomers use to detect exoplanets. The team tested this approach using the Allen Telescope Array, collecting data from 2024 to 2026, which detected 1.9 million radio signals, though none were extraterrestrial. Additional data from 121 nights remains unreleased. Challenges include the antisolar point’s changing position and uncertainty about whether aliens would use the same method. The approach aims to narrow search efforts rather than scanning space randomly.

item.title: Smartphone Makers Use Recycled Memory to Cope with Shortages
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Memory shortage spurs smartphone makers to melt used memory off old devices, then re-solder it onto new products
Smartphone manufacturers are increasingly using reballed memory—recycled chips from older devices—to address memory shortages and cut costs. TrendForce reports current adoption is 3–4%, rising to 7–9% by 2027. Reballed memory involves melting and re-soldering used chips, enabling reuse in new devices. This practice helps offset rising bill of materials costs, allowing budget phones priced below CNY 1,299 ($200) to remain affordable. As DRAM prices are expected to climb in 2027, manufacturers may expand reballed memory use beyond entry-level models. Hardware hobbyists also repurpose memory, with one converting a $120 DDR5 SO-DIMM kit into a $1,000 desktop memory setup. Both industries and enthusiasts face technical challenges in reballing, but the trend highlights efforts to reuse memory amid supply constraints and high costs.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Apple Watch Health Alerts Help Seniors Stay Safe
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Every senior with an Apple Watch should set up these 5 health alerts
Apple Watch health alerts help seniors stay safe. Emergency SOS, Fall Detection, Crash Detection, heart health monitoring, and medication reminders are key features. Emergency SOS contacts services when needed, requiring a cellular plan or nearby iPhone. Fall Detection calls emergency services after detecting immobility post-fall, activated via Health app settings. Crash Detection alerts after car crashes. Heart health features include continuous monitoring, ECG readings, and alerts for abnormal heart rates. Medication Reminders track doses via Health app. Sleep Apnea notifications and Sound Recognition for doorbells/sirens aid seniors. Accessibility tools adjust font size for visually impaired users. CDC data highlights fall risks, with 319,000 older adults hospitalized for hip fractures annually. Pew Research notes 26% of US seniors live alone, increasing fall risks. These features support independent living and health management for older adults.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 6 Linux boot options that can save you from a broken system
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Linux users can recover from system failures using six boot options. Roll back a kernel update by selecting an older kernel version via GRUB's Advanced options. Use systemd rescue mode to access a minimal environment for repairing configuration files or removing problematic packages. Emergency mode provides a root shell for troubleshooting filesystem or mount issues. Disable a problematic systemd service with the systemd.mask parameter. Boot directly into a Bash root shell using init=/bin/bash to bypass systemd. Disable early graphics mode with nomodeset to bypass driver issues. These methods help users investigate and fix startup problems without reinstalling. Tools like Timeshift and Snapper can create snapshots for quick recovery from failed updates.

item.title: Apple sells $50 AI usage packs for Creator Studio apps
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Apple starts offering $50 extended usage packs for AI features in Creator Studio
Apple is selling $50 intelligence usage packs for Creator Studio users to access AI features beyond monthly limits. Logic Pro, updated last month, includes an AI assistant powered by Apple and third-party models. Users can view AI usage via the app's menu bar and purchase additional packs through the 'Buy More Usage' option. Packs are available to subscribers in the US, UK, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, India, and Mexico, tied to individual Apple accounts with no Family Sharing. Unused packs roll over monthly and expire 12 months after purchase. Additional usage applies only after reaching monthly limits. Apple may expand packs to other Creator Studio apps like Final Cut Pro and Pixelmator Pro. Creator Studio apps are available via subscription or one-time purchase. The company previously outlined plans for expanded AI access through iCloud+ but now offers this as a standalone purchase option.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to turn on personal results on your Google Home
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Google Home now offers personal results via Voice Match, allowing users to access tailored information like calendars and notes. Setup requires linking Google accounts and enabling Voice Match through the Google Home app. Personal results work with Gemini-powered devices, letting users ask for personalized data such as to-do lists or music playlists. Up to six family members can set up individual profiles, each with their own voice recognition. Without Voice Match, personal data is accessible to all users. The feature ensures responses are unique to the speaker, with examples including reminders for school tests or grocery lists. Users must configure Voice Match for each person in the household to enable personalized interactions. Privacy notes warn that disabling Voice Match exposes personal results to others, requiring additional steps for shared devices in common areas.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old electronics can be restored but CRTs require caution
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Old consoles, stereos, and PCs are worth restoring, but leave the CRT alone
Old consoles, stereos, and PCs can be restored with basic repairs, but CRTs require caution. A Game Boy can be upgraded with an IPS display requiring minimal soldering, while older consoles often need cleaning and capacitor checks. Stereo gear typically requires belt and capacitor replacements, but capacitors in receivers can hold lethal charges. Old computers should have their power supplies inspected for cracked capacitors before use. CRTs, like 27-inch displays, operate at 27,000 volts and contain toxic materials like beryllium and cadmium, making them dangerous for inexperienced restorers. A 25W soldering iron and service manual are essential tools for most repairs. Professionals are advised for CRT work due to high voltage and toxicity risks.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Google Wallet Adds Notification Feed, Allows Disabling
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How does Google Wallet's notification feed work and can you disable it?
Google Wallet introduced a notification feed in October 2026 as part of an update aimed at competing with Apple Wallet. The feature includes a bell icon in the app's top-right corner, accessible via the profile icon. Notifications aggregate updates about saved cards, travel changes, loyalty programs, and offers. Users can manage notifications through Wallet settings or app permissions. To disable all notifications, settings can be adjusted under 'Manage Wallet Notifications' or by turning off location access in app permissions. The feed is still being rolled out, so not all users may see it immediately.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Enhanced AI Models for Coding, Research, and Cybersecurity
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, The Verge, Gizmodo Original headline: Anthropic Unveils Enhanced AI Models for Coding, Research, and Cybersecurity
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, advanced AI models with improved coding, research, and cybersecurity capabilities. Fable 5.2 achieved 49.1% on the FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, surpassing its 5.1 version, and solved black hole physics problems while formalizing Fermat’s Last Theorem proof. It also designed electronic devices, completed software migrations, and coordinated 1,000 AI agents to build a bootable operating system. Mythos 5.2 scored 89.6% on the CVE Rediscovery benchmark but is restricted to vetted organizations. Gizmodo raised concerns about past risks, including cyberattacks and fake identities, though Anthropic claims alignment improvements. The models’ capabilities have sparked debate over AI’s role in scientific discovery, with some findings remaining unpeer-reviewed. Pricing at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens reflects reduced costs compared to prior versions.

item.title: Brits distrust banks' fraud prevention amid AI threats
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Most Brits don't think their bank is doing a good job at stopping fraud
Most Brits distrust their banks' ability to stop fraud, with 69% believing banks can't detect AI deepfakes impersonating them. Four in five expect improved ID verification tools within five years, though convenience remains a priority. Over half (53%) say one-time security codes are no longer sufficient. Banks face pressure to balance security and speed, with 62% willing to tolerate only two extra minutes of checks. Despite concerns, 79% expect smoother verification processes. However, banks rely on third-party providers, leaving them vulnerable to reputational damage if verification fails. Digidentity UK's Jonathan Evans notes banks bear responsibility for providers' errors. The Bank of England has urged social media firms to combat scams, highlighting growing threats to both consumers and businesses.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Starlink Leaks Mini 2 Dish Price at $249
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: $249? Starlink's Website Reportedly Leaks Mini 2 Dish's Price
Starlink's website appears to have leaked pricing for the second-gen Mini dish. DISHYtech discovered mentions of 'Mini 2 Beta' and 'Mini 2 Beta Kit' in backend API code, indicating a beta rollout for select users. The product is priced at $249, matching the first-gen Mini's retail price. A separate 'us-mini-2-battery-beta' entry suggests a $50 battery add-on for extended connectivity, unlike the first-gen model. The code references appear in the Starlink shop for existing subscribers and were also found in firmware updates. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk showcased the Mini 2 alongside the V5 dish in June. The findings are based on code analysis, though replication was not confirmed. The first-gen Mini is currently discounted to $149 on Starlink.com.

item.title: Fervo Secures $12B in Geothermal Power Orders
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Fervo now has $12B in orders for its geothermal power tech
Fervo, a geothermal energy company, reported $11.9 billion in contracted revenue for its third-quarter earnings, up from $7.2 billion the previous quarter. The company is completing a 396-megawatt power plant for Google by 2028 and connected its first 100-megawatt plant to the grid this year. Both projects are at Cape Station in Utah, a site capable of generating 8.4 gigawatts of electricity, surpassing earlier estimates of 4 gigawatts. CEO Tim Latimer noted the phased construction allows Google to develop data centers independently. Fervo’s GeoBlocks, each generating up to 50 megawatts, are designed to match data center demand. Despite an operating loss of $43.7 million, Fervo holds $1.9 billion in cash and $301.6 million in debt. The Google project costs $5,500 per kilowatt, down from $7,000, with potential to reach $3,000 per kilowatt long-term, making it competitive with natural gas. Google’s early investment highlights confidence in Fervo’s cost reduction trajectory.

item.title: Apple completes AI registration for iPads and Macs in China
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple Intelligence just cleared another major roadblock in China, and Macs are next
Apple has completed regulatory registration for its AI features on iPads and notebooks in China, advancing its rollout beyond iPhones. Shanghai’s cyberspace regulator confirmed on November 9 that Apple Intelligence is now registered for use on tablets and notebook computers, removing a key hurdle after nearly two years of navigating China’s AI regulations. The initial iPhone release is set for December with iOS 27.3, but iPadOS and macOS versions remain pending approval. Apple’s partnership with Alibaba will integrate Qwen-powered capabilities into features like Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence. While the latest approval covers laptops, desktop Macs’ status is unclear. The move brings Apple’s AI ecosystem closer to full device compatibility in China, though exact release dates for iPads and Macs are still pending.

item.title: Instagram launches AI tool to create custom filter effects
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
Instagram is launching Effect Builder, an AI tool that generates custom filters for Stories. Available to U.S. residents over 18, the tool lets users describe filter ideas via text prompts and attach style reference images. Users can preview AI-generated effects, refine them with follow-up prompts, and submit filters for Instagram’s safety review. The AI can rewrite prompts, as seen when a test request to turn photos into comic book pages resulted in detailed style specifications. Approved filters appear in Stories, with links back to the creator’s profile. Filters must pass safety checks before being shared. The tool expands Instagram’s editing capabilities beyond its Edits app, which recently launched on macOS.

item.title: Ransomware group BYOD claims breach of Vanderbilt University data
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Attackers Claim to Have Stolen Data on Over 1 Million Vanderbilt Students and Staff
Vanderbilt University faced a ransomware attack attributed to the group BYOD, which claimed to have stolen data on over a million students and staff. The attack prompted officials to order all users to disconnect from the campus Wi-Fi network and shut down devices to prevent further damage. Affected individuals reported encrypted files and inaccessible research data, with some professors canceling classes despite university assurances that operations would continue. A ransom message published on Ransomware.live detailed the stolen data, including Social Security numbers, contact information, and system access. BYOD, a group known for previous attacks on Michigan State University and the University of New Mexico Health System, mocked the university’s 'Bring Your Own Device' policy, which critics argue increases security risks. Vanderbilt’s press office did not immediately comment, and the attack is linked to a similar incident at the Texas Health and Human Services Commission, per DataBreach.com.

item.title: Honor 700 series phones debut with rear health display
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Honor's 700 series gets a rear display, too: early teasers show a focus on the heart
Honor's 700 series phones, set to launch November 13, feature a rear display with health tracking capabilities. Tipster Digital Chat Station claims the devices include a 6.5-inch screen with thin bezels, mini-games, dynamic notifications, and a 200MP camera. The rear display shows heart rate and blood oxygen levels, though details remain unconfirmed. The series includes three models: 700, 700 Pro, and 700S. The 600 Pro used a Snapdragon 8 Elite, while the base model had a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4. Specs vary by model, with no confirmed details yet. Analysts note the 600 series was mid-range, and pricing concerns persist due to market conditions. Honor follows up quickly on the 600 series, which launched in April. The 700 series may offer similar features but with potential variations.

item.title: AI hardware startup Nominal triples valuation to $3B in 8 months
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Nominal, an Austin-based AI hardware startup, raised $240 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation, tripling its worth in eight months. The round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by Insight Partners. This follows a $155 million Series B extension in March at a $1 billion valuation, led by Founders Fund. The Series B was a preemptive deal initiated by investors. Other backers include Sequoia, General Catalyst, and Lux Capital. Nominal serves 80 commercial and government clients, including defense firm Anduril, co-founded by Founders Fund’s Trae Stephens. The company secured a $71.2 million Air Force STRATFI contract in October, requiring matching funds. CEO Cameron McCord, a former U.S. Navy submarine officer and Anduril alum, leads the firm. The funding underscores growing interest in AI-driven hardware testing for sectors like aerospace and defense.

item.title: Samsung Develops AI App to Organize Saved Content
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Samsung is working on a new Galaxy AI app to clean up the screenshot mess you’ve been pretending doesn’t exist
Samsung is developing an AI-powered app called Memory to help users organize saved content. The app allows users to collect screenshots, links, text, and voice notes in one place, with AI automatically generating titles, summaries, and tags to group related items into collections. Features include shortcuts for content capture, such as a three-finger swipe for screenshots and a button combo for voice notes. Memory also recognizes web page screenshots and retrieves original links. The app is expected to launch with One UI 9.5, though no official release date has been confirmed. Samsung highlights privacy measures, stating content is processed locally but some advanced features require online processing. The app addresses common frustrations with fragmented saved data across apps. Similar tools exist on Google’s Pixel and Oppo’s Mind Space, but Samsung’s Memory is the first of its kind on Galaxy devices. The app aims to enhance daily tasks like research and planning by providing a searchable, organized space for saved information.

item.title: Camera Makers Partner with Phone Brands to Boost Smartphone Imaging
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Why do camera makers partner on phones? I toured ARRI to find out
Smartphone makers collaborate with camera companies to enhance smartphone imaging. Partnerships like Nokia-Zeiss, Huawei-Leica, and now Honor-ARRI reflect a strategic shift to leverage camera expertise. ARRI, known for filmmaking cameras, partners with Honor to focus on video quality, color science, and LUT profiles. The Honor Magic 9 Pro Max and Robot Phone feature ARRI-branded modes, allowing real-time preview of color grading effects. ARRI’s labs emphasize precision and quality, with cameras used in 17 of the last 20 Best Picture winners. The partnership aims to introduce ARRI’s technology to younger filmmakers and reduce costs for location scouting. While hardware limitations prevent ARRI from making smartphone cameras, the collaboration offers insights into color processing and expands ARRI’s reach. Both companies see potential for growth, with Honor gaining expertise and ARRI accessing new audiences. The partnership highlights a trend where traditional camera makers adapt to smartphone markets, blending high-end imaging with mobile accessibility.

item.title: X enables video clipping without downloads or external apps
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: X finally lets you clip videos without downloading them or using another app
X introduced a new feature allowing users to clip videos without downloading or using external apps. The update lets creators earn credit and revenue from clips, which now link back to original content. Previously, users had to download, edit, and re-upload videos, often leaving original creators unpaid. Clips must be 5-60 seconds, not exceeding 30% of the original video’s length. Livestreams cannot be clipped yet, though support is planned. Users can tap the Repost icon, select 'Clip video,' and trim segments. Both creators and clipper can earn money via X’s Original Content Rewards program. The change streamlines the process, making it faster and more profitable for all parties involved.

item.title: Russian Hosting Firm Beget Hit by Major Cyberattack
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'We are not giving up': Russian hosting giant Beget has cloud platform wiped in major cyberattack
Russian hosting provider Beget suffered a major cyberattack on November 1st, 2026, wiping cloud storage, VPS hosting, Kubernetes servers, and thousands of websites. The attack coincided with a wave of drone and online strikes targeting Russian tech firms, likely by Ukraine-based actors or anti-Putin groups. Beget’s infrastructure was fully disabled, requiring over 1,000 servers to be manually inspected for damage. The company confirmed data recovery from backups is possible but warned the process will take weeks. Beget faces EU sanctions for hosting Russian-occupied Ukraine regions. A compliance expert warned of systemic risks from over-reliance on a single provider. Founded in 2007, Beget holds 14.7% of Russia’s .ru domain market. Customers were urged to update credentials after the breach. The attack’s motive—whether linked to sanctions or standalone cybercrime—remains unclear.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: iPhone 5C searches surge 40,500% as retro tech trend takes off
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
Searches for 'buy iPhone 5C' have surged 40,500% in the past year, driven by Gen Z’s interest in retro cameras and the Y2K aesthetic. The iPhone 5C, released in 2013, is praised for its 8MP camera, which appeals to users seeking vintage-style photography. However, security experts warn of risks due to the device’s outdated software. Lee Elliott of Compare and Recycle notes the iPhone 5C can only run iOS 10.3.3, last updated in 2017, leaving it vulnerable to data breaches and hacking. To mitigate risks, Elliott recommends using the phone offline, without a SIM card or Apple ID, and transferring photos via cable instead of cloud storage. If online access is needed, a disposable Apple ID should be used for non-sensitive tasks. Users are advised to avoid logging into personal accounts like email or banking. Despite the risks, the iPhone 5C remains a popular choice for its retro appeal and camera capabilities.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Wyndham exposed customer data via hardcoded app password
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Hotel giant Wyndham exposed customer data after app security lapse
Wyndham exposed customer data after a security researcher found a hardcoded password in its Android app, granting access to a Salesforce-hosted database containing personal information. Robert Wiggins, a security researcher, revealed the credential allowed access to customer names, emails, member numbers, and login tokens. The database also included internal files, though the exact number of affected records remains unclear. Wyndham, which has 129 million rewards members, declined to confirm if it would notify customers or report the breach to regulators. A spokesperson stated there was no evidence of unauthorized access but would not detail past access checks or plans for a vulnerability disclosure program. Wiggins noted the password was likely embedded for an undetermined period and criticized the lack of long-term fixes. This follows a 2024 incident where Wyndham hotels ran spyware leaking guest data, leading to the arrest of owner Bryan Fleming for selling illegal spyware.
